learning_outcomes.text: Students learn about the influence of cyclic loads on material behavior and can assess the influence of cracks on component behavior.
Can evaluate the influence of various constructive boundary conditions on fatigue strength.
Can establish connections between damage patterns of fracture surfaces and fatigue stresses.
Understand selected testing methods for cyclic loading and can experimentally determine relevant characteristic values for component design.
Develop skills to calculate the lifespan of cyclically loaded components under multi-stage, real operating stresses using simple examples.
Learn aspects of fracture mechanics and, based on this, can consider the influence of cracks in component design under cyclic loading.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of fatigue behavior, especially of metallic materials
Notch effect and influence on fatigue strength
Other selected influencing factors on fatigue strength
Concepts (Miner's rule) for lifetime prediction under single- and multi-stage cyclic loads
Special material tests under cyclic loading (fatigue tests, fracture mechanics)
Counting methods and lifetime prediction for real stress-time functions
Application of fracture mechanics in lifetime prediction under cyclic loads

assessment_methods.method: Practical course: active participation in all dates

assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination and proof of performance. The successful participation in the practical course is achieved through active student participation in all practical course dates. The grading influences the final grade according to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
